entry.title: DYNAS: A Dynamic Network Penetration Testing Framework Using Deep Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
As network scale and uncertainty complicate automated penetration testing, reinforcement learning (RL) environments must support controlled evaluation under defensive and non-stationary conditions. We present DYNAS (Dynamic Network Attack Simulator), which combines parameterized large-scale scenario generation with stateful intrusion detection responses, explicit scan false-positive and false-negative noise, temporary service unavailability, and duration-based action timeouts. We further introduce Pen-DHRL, a recurrent manager--worker policy that selects persistent subgoals using IDS-conditioned global context.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #ml-theory

entry.title: RV2GC: Reconstructing the Garbling Boundary in a RISC-V Garbled Processor
entry.summary:
Programmable garbled-circuit execution must balance the benefits of cross-program reuse against the cost of repeated work during secure execution. A complete garbled processor provides a fixed circuit for many programs, but its evaluator repeatedly visits processor-wide structures even when only a small part performs the current protected computation. We present RV2GC, which reconstructs the garbling boundary around a fixed library of RISC-V instruction circuits.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #semiconductors

entry.title: Systematic Evaluation of Adversarial Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses Across Seven Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Large language models (LLMs) deployed in safety-critical settings must resist adversarial inputs designed to elicit harmful outputs. We present a systematic empirical evaluation of five adversarial jailbreaking attack families---direct requests, roleplay-based jailbreaking, hypothetical framing, instruction override, and obfuscation---across seven open-weight and API-accessible LLMs: Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma2-9B, and Phi-4-14B. We further evaluate four defense mechanisms: keyword blacklisting, self-reminder prompting, paraphrase-based sanitization, and perplexity-based filtering against the two most vulnerable models.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: ACORN-QRE: Specification and Analysis of a Method of Generating Secure One-time Pads for Use in Encryption
entry.summary:
REAMC Report-007(2023) [Reissued October 2026 with modified licence CC BY-NC-ND; no other changes] ACORN-QRE: Specification and Analysis of a Method of Generating Secure One-time Pads for Use in Encryption Roy S Wikramaratna (email: rwikramaratna@gmail.com) Abstract The Additive Congruential Random Number (ACORN) generator is straightforward to implement; it has been demonstrated in previous papers to give rise to sequences with long period which can be proven from theoretical considerations to approximate to being uniform in up to k dimensions (for any given k). The ACORN-QRE algorithm is a straightforward modification of ACORN which effectively avoids the linearity of the original algorithm, while preserving the uniformity of the modified sequence. It provides a new method for generating one-time pads that are resistant to attack either by current computers or by future computing developments, including quantum computers.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Leakage-Diagrams, Importance Sampling, and Composition in the Random Probing Model
entry.summary:
Security evaluation of masking in low-noise regimes remains poorly understood: increasing the masking order does not automatically translate into higher concrete resistance once many correlated intermediates are processed by a full implementation. A common approach is to reduce noisy side-channel leakage to the random probing model (RPM), but existing reductions can be too loose to yield meaningful leakage rates in practice, and current RPM analyses often rely on costly simulations or numerically propagated bounds. This work develops analytic and algorithmic tools for estimating and upper-bounding RPM security of masked gadgets and their compositions.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Morphic Accumulators and Applications: Optimal Range Proofs, Polynomial Commitments, and Ring Signatures
entry.summary:
Cryptographic accumulators based on groups of unknown order (GUO) provide constant-size set membership proofs. For security purposes, existing works require first encoding set elements via division-intractable (DI) hash functions, typically instantiated as random oracles that destroy any algebraic structure. This confines GUO-based accumulators to a purely set-membership role, making them "incompatible" with various existing cryptographic proof techniques over committed integers in the same groups as the GUO, such as constant-size proofs of exponentiation and modular exponent relations.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: A Spectral Theory of Local-to-Global Leakage
entry.summary:
This paper studies how local leakages characterize the global leakage in additive secret sharing over a finite abelian group, which is a special case of linear secret sharing and side-channel masking. Our main finding is structural: local-to-global leakage is governed by two disjoint components---the magnitude of local leakage and its spectral alignment across shares, while existing literature attempted to characterize the global leakage only by local mutual information (MI). We first give an exact decomposition of leakage in additive secret sharing.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #logic

entry.title: Indistinguishability Obfuscation via Mathematical Proofs of Equivalence. Over the last decade, indistinguishability obfuscation (iO) has emerged as a seemingly omnipotent primitive in cryptography.
entry.summary:
Over the last decade, indistinguishability obfuscation (iO) has emerged as a seemingly omnipotent primitive in cryptography. Moreover, recent breakthrough work has demonstrated that iO can be realized from well-founded assumptions. A thorn to all this remarkable progress is a limitation of all known constructions of general-purpose iO: the security reduction incurs a loss that is exponential in the input length of the function.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: How To Think About End-To-End Encryption and AI: Training, Processing, Disclosure, and Consent
entry.summary:
End-to-end encryption (E2EE) has become the gold standard for securing communications, bringing strong confidentiality and privacy guarantees to billions of users worldwide. However, the current push towards widespread integration of artificial intelligence (AI) models, including in E2EE systems, raises some serious security concerns. This work performs a critical examination of the (in)compatibility of AI models and E2EE applications.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
